headline: Broad egress on both agents creates medium leakage and conflict risk; no documented shared channel makes prompt-injection and cascading-error lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte exposes an Airbyte API and broad network egress, while Plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and config file surface. No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced; the only plausible bridge is manual or orchestrated content transfer, which is lower risk.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte-produced text into Plano prompts without review, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Require human review before copying outputs between agents.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared queue integration.
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from transferred text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and agentic signals and also has broad egress. A shared OS workspace is not documented, but if one is introduced, either agent could move sensitive operational data off-box through its outbound API path, making leakage plausible in default-style deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same directory or mounted volume, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is configured to send file contents or logs to its backend, sensitive data can leave the host.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace by default.
Redact logs, traces, and business data before transfer.
Restrict outbound destinations with an allowlist.
Rotate or minimize retained logs in Plano.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and Plano can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; both have broad network egress, so they can contend over shared mutable remote resources if pointed at the same service. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, and Plano explicitly does not support multiple instances, increasing the chance of operational contention.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same API-backed dataset or queue, conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator runs them concurrently without locks, last-writer-wins behavior is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate target resources per agent.
Serialize writes with an external lock.
Use read-only credentials where possible.
Monitor for duplicate or conflicting writes.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data and Plano can consume and route model outputs through its chat-completions endpoint. Because no verification or critique loop is documented between them, one agent’s output can become the other’s input and propagate errors into downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is fed directly into Plano prompts or routing rules, errors can cascade.
IF Plano is used to act on Airbyte-derived summaries without validation, downstream mistakes can spread.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require schema checks on Airbyte outputs.
Have Plano cite source records before acting.
Sample and compare outputs against raw inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte is documented as handling business data, while Plano is documented as handling logs, traces, metrics, and agentic signals. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to a generic gap rather than a specific violation; the two profiles do not show a direct regulated-data conflict.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through either agent, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF retention policies differ for the same dataset, a mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Avoid sending regulated data to either agent.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Review residency and DPA requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
